content:
- Overestimate prices in early forecast windows when sentiment is positive (especially >0.3) — model tends to overshoot.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is weak or negative (sentiment <0.2) — model fails to capture downward momentum.
- Model exhibits lag in correcting for recent price drops — true values often dip below forecast before rebounding.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior day), model overreacts and forecasts higher than true — apply downward correction by 10–15% of spike magnitude.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show high sentiment + rising prices, model overweights trend; correct by reducing forecast slope.
- Forecast horizon 30d: model tends to overestimate mid-term decline after strong sentiment drop — adjust downward by 2–4% for sentiment <0.25.
- Sentiment >0.4 correlates with forecast overconfidence — reduce forecast by 3–5% if sentiment >0.4 and price is rising.
